title: School Cleaner
description:
About the Role

The Priory School is seeking to recruit a Cleaner to join our team.

The post is part-time (12.5 hours per week) and the hours will be 3.30-6pm Monday to Friday, term time only.

The salary is £25,614 pro rata.

If you are interested in applying, please complete and submit the application form.

The closing date for applications is 9am on Tuesday 24th November. Interviews will take place later that week.

The Priory School, Hitchin

The Priory School is an oversubscribed, co-educational Foundation School serving over 1,200 students in the Hertfordshire town of Hitchin. As part of the Hitchin Sixth Form Consortium (alongside Hitchin Girls’ School and Hitchin Boys’ School), we also offer access to a vibrant post-16 community of over 800 learners.

Our values

At The Priory School, Hitchin, we are committed to empowering every child to meet their aspirations, to be self-confident, inspirational, and active members of their community whatever their background, ability, or circumstance. We achieve this by ensuring that every child at TPSH follows a rich and ambitious curriculum, is offered extensive extra-curricular and enrichment opportunities, and that they benefit from inspirational teaching, alongside dedicated pastoral care that provides a secure and caring environment.

We are incredibly proud of our students who are superb ambassadors for our school when representing us in Hitchin but also nationally, and internationally. We are proud to serve the entire community of Hitchin and as such, we have a number of exciting partnerships with local and national organisations.

Our staff are well-qualified, highly experienced, and dedicated to providing the very best education and pastoral care to every student. We all share the same values that are woven into our school’s culture: Responsibility, Respect, and Resilience.

Staff development and support

We are committed to providing high-quality professional development and support to all of our staff and understand that teachers and support staff are the decisive element in positively changing the lives of young people.

We offer an extensive wrap-around support framework for our teachers, ensuring you have the mentoring, resources, and leadership guidance to excel and advance your career. We recognise that teaching is a rewarding but pressured profession; as such, we are dedicated to maintaining a culture where staff wellbeing matters. In staff surveys, our staff consistently report that they are proud to work at The Priory School, Hitchin.

Facilities

Our school has some of the best facilities that you will find anywhere and we are lucky enough to sit on an expansive 27-acre site. We benefitted from a £1.6 million investment in our 3G football pitches in collaboration with Hitchin Belles Football Club, a £500,000 pavilion, revamped café, a new languages block, and our newly built Sixth Form centre which received a £2.8million investment. We also have ample on-site parking and are a short walk from Hitchin train station.

Working or living in Hitchin

Hitchin is a beautiful historic market town in North Hertfordshire, surrounded by lovely countryside, with a population of approximately 33,500. It has been voted in the ‘Top 10 Best Places to Live in the UK’ in The Times.

It has great transport links, being just two miles from the A1(M) and only 10 miles from the M1, and is in easy reach of London with Kings Cross station a mere 30 minutes away. There is also good access to the main rail routes to Cambridge.

The town is great for families with lots of activities for young people and their parents to participate in including sports and activities, youth organisations, performing arts and more. Hitchin also is well known in the area as a town for foodies with virtually every cuisine represented. Hitchin Festival runs throughout the month of July with over 100 different events celebrating the artistic, cultural and community life of the town.

Applying for this role

If you are interested in working at our school and would like further information, please contact Emma Sangster (esangster@priory.herts.sch.uk; 01462 422300).

If you would like to apply for the post, please submit the application form electronically to Emma Sangster (esangster@priory.herts.sch.uk) or submit via MyNewTerm.

The Priory School, Hitchin is fully committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff to share this commitment. An enhanced DBS disclosure will be sought for the successful candidate in accordance with Safeguarding Children and Safer Recruitment in Education legislation.

title: Pathways to Employment Officer (Southampton)
description:
Are you passionate about helping adults overcome barriers and move confidently into work, training or further learning? Here at Brockenhurst College we are seeking a dedicated Pathways to Employment Officer to join our dynamic Employment Services team at QuickStart based in Southampton. This role requires a candidate with a full driving licence and access to a reliable vehicle for essential travel. This is a permanent part time position where Wednesday and Thursday availability is essential to ensure coverage with their job share counterpart. The remaining hours are flexible and open to discussion. In this impactful role, you'll provide high quality information, advice and guidance (IAG), personalised employability support to unemployed adults referred through Jobcentre Plus, local councils and community partners. You will build participants’ confidence, develop their skills, broker meaningful job opportunities and support their journey into sustainable employment. Working within a collaborative, forward thinking environment, you’ll also contribute to classroom and assessment delivery, partnership engagement and maintaining excellent standards of quality, compliance and learner experience. In return you will receive a salary of £24,834 - £27,211 per annum (pro rata) DOE.If you’re motivated, organised and committed to making a real difference in people’s lives, we’d love you to join our team.

The Pathways to Employment Officer Role:

To provide high‑quality information, advice and guidance (IAG) and employability support to unemployed adults and jobseekers referred via Jobcentre Plus/DWP, local authorities and community partners. The role builds work‑readiness, brokers sustainable job outcomes, and supports learners in and out of the classroom. The postholder will undertake associated learner administration, partner liaison and compliance checks, ensuring learners are placed on the most appropriate programme based on their current level, learning needs and funding eligibility. The postholder will also invigilate assessments/exams when required and contribute to Initial Provider Interviews (IPIs) and job club activity to agreed standards and compliance requirements.

Responsibilities as our Pathways to Employment Officer will include:

Participant engagement, assessment & planning

  • Contribute to IPIs and ongoing reviews to assess needs, employability level, and barriers; co‑create action plans with SMART goals and agreed next steps.
  • Triage and onboard participants from Jobcentre Plus/DWP, councils, and community referrals; manage a dynamic caseload to timely outcomes.
  • Provide impartial IAG aligned to the Matrix Standard ethos and college policies, ensuring appropriate signposting (wellbeing, housing, finance, ESOL, SEND).

Employability support & job search coaching

  • Deliver one‑to‑one and small‑group sessions on CVs, applications, digital job search, interview skills, labour‑market awareness, and soft‑skills (confidence, resilience, teamwork).
  • Track progress to milestones (engagement, skills gain, interviews, job starts, sustainment), adapting plans as needs change.

Employer engagement

  • Proactively source vacancies, work trials, sector‑based work academies (SWAP‑style), and volunteering/experience with local employers.
  • Prepare candidates and match them to roles; organise employer talks, mock interviews, and recruitment events; support offer/induction and in‑work sustainment.

Multi‑agency partnership working

  • Maintain effective working relationships with Jobcentre Plus/DWP Work Coaches, local councils, community organisations, and training providers to coordinate referrals, co‑location, and joint interventions.
  • Represent the college at local employability forums, task groups, and job fairs; share labour‑market intelligence and pipeline opportunities with colleagues.

Classroom support & invigilation

  • Support tutors in the classroom with employability, study skills, and work‑readiness content; provide on‑programme IAG and progression guidance.
  • On occasion invigilate assessments/exams in line with awarding‑body and college regulations (room setup, ID checks, security, incident reporting, scripts handling).
  • Provide targeted wrap‑around support for learners at risk of withdrawal or non‑completion, liaising with curriculum, ALS/SEND and safeguarding teams.

Compliance, quality & data

  • Maintain accurate, timely records of IPIs, action plans, attendance, outcomes and evidence on college MIS/CRM and (where required) DWP/council systems.
  • Adhere to funding and audit requirements (e.g., eligibility checks, residency/evidence, outcome verification), GDPR, safeguarding, Prevent, EDI and Health & Safety.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement (self‑assessment, learner voice, observations of practice, CPD).

Performance & results

  • Meet or exceed KPIs: engagement, timely IPI completion, progression to learning, job starts, sustained outcomes (e.g., 13/26 weeks), employer satisfaction, and data quality.
  • Produce concise, insight‑driven reports and case studies for managers and co-ordinators

As our Pathways to Employment Officer, you’ll ideally have:

  • Level 2 English & Maths (or equivalent) – Essential
  • Driving licence and access to transport for outreach
  • L3+ Advice & Guidance (IAG) or Careers (e.g., L3 CIAG) – Desirable / or willingness to achieve.
  • One‑to‑one and group employability/IAG support with unemployed adults or adult learners.
  • Working with Jobcentre Plus/DWP, local councils or employability programmes (e.g., Restart, WHP, Multiply, adult skills).
  • Employer engagement and job matching; organising recruitment events and interviews.
  • Classroom or workshop delivery alongside tutors; assessment or invigilation procedures.
  • Caseload management with outcome targets and robust record‑keeping.
  • Knowledge of local labour‑market trends and priority sectors; barriers faced by jobseekers.
  • Knowledge of Funding/compliance in FE/employability settings (ESFA/DWP expectations); data protection (GDPR).
  • Knowledge of Safeguarding, Prevent and inclusive practice, including reasonable adjustments and trauma‑informed approaches.

If you feel you are the right candidate for this Pathways to Employment Officer role, then please click ‘apply’ now!

Closing Date: 4 December 2026

title: Academy Administrator
description:
Join Pimlico Primary Academy as an Academy Administrator and play a key role in supporting the smooth and effective running of our school community.

About this Role

We are seeking an organised, proactive and approachable Academy Administrator to join our team at Pimlico Primary Academy.

This is a varied and rewarding role, offering the opportunity to work closely with school leaders, colleagues, pupils and families, whilst contributing to the delivery of a high-quality administrative service.

As Academy Administrator, you will play an integral role in the day-to-day operations of the academy, providing effective administrative support, maintaining accurate records and ensuring a professional and welcoming environment for pupils, parents, colleagues and visitors. You will also support the academy in maintaining its high standards of safeguarding, compliance and operational efficiency.

The successful candidate will be a highly organised individual with excellent interpersonal and communication skills, strong attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities. You will demonstrate professionalism, discretion and a proactive approach to your work, recognising the important role that effective administration plays in a successful school.

About Us

Pimlico Primary Academy is a primary school in the heart of Westminster and is proud to be part of Future Academies, a flourishing multi-academy trust founded with the aim of improving the life chances and raising the aspirations of young people.

Since opening in September 2013, the academy has focused on providing children with an exceptional start to their education, establishing strong academic foundations alongside confidence, character and aspiration.

Our carefully sequenced, knowledge-rich curriculum is designed to foster intellectual curiosity and a lasting enthusiasm for learning. Purpose-built facilities, outdoor spaces and our close relationship with neighbouring Pimlico Academy contribute to a stimulating educational environment.

Guided by our Trust values of Knowledge, Aspiration and Respect, we encourage pupils to take pride in their learning, develop independence and approach new experiences with confidence. Clear expectations and caring relationships help create purposeful classrooms.

Our teachers and support staff work together to shape children’s earliest educational experiences. Joining Pimlico Primary offers the opportunity to contribute to a school community that values strong relationships, academic purpose and the development of every child.

At Future Academies, we recognise that our employees are our greatest asset and play a vital role in the success of our schools. We are committed to creating a supportive and rewarding working environment where colleagues feel valued.

To support this commitment, we offer a range of employee benefits, including:

  1. A supportive working environment with a strong commitment to colleague wellbeing.
  2. Excellent continuing professional development (CPD) opportunities and career progression.
  3. Employer contributions to the Local Government Pension Scheme.
  4. Mintago – access to a range of employee benefits and savings, including childcare cost savings.
  5. An Employee Assistance Programme, providing confidential support and guidance.
  6. Access to a Virtual GP service.

Ready to Join Us?

If you are a motivated and organised individual who enjoys building relationships, working collaboratively and making a positive difference within a school community, we would love to hear from you.

This is a fantastic opportunity to join a supportive and dedicated team, take ownership of a varied workload and play an important role in supporting the continued success of Pimlico Primary Academy.

We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds and are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workforce.

Prospective candidates are encouraged to visit our academy to experience our school community and learn more about the role.

If you believe you have the skills, experience and enthusiasm to succeed in this role, we encourage you to apply and look forward to receiving your application.

Please refer to the attached recruitment pack for the full job description and person specification.

Applications must be received by 12:00 pm on Tuesday 1 December 2026. Applications received after this deadline will not be considered.

description:
This is a very exciting opportunity for a dedicated and passionate Forest School Lead to join our Trust to provide a quality Forest Schools provision for our specialist provisions across the Trust.

You will be a highly skilled and reflective practitioner, committed to supporting exceptional SEND provision and achieving the best possible outcomes for all pupils.

We welcome applications from both qualified Forest School practitioners who have experience within SEND education settings as well as those from mainstream settings with a passion for Special Educational Needs and a proven track record of supporting pupils with SEND. You will be adaptable and resilient, with an understanding of how to contribute effectively to the existing positive culture and ethos of our welcoming and inclusive school communities. Experience of working with children with additional needs in a primary or Early Years setting is essential. We offer excellent opportunities for professional development and expect all staff to be committed to continually improving their practice and developing their careers.

You will be committed to the highest standards of achievement for all. You will be a resourceful, inclusive and enthusiastic Forest School Lead, with a strong understanding of strategies that support positive pupil outcomes, particularly where communication and interaction needs, including autism spectrum condition (ASC), are a primary focus.

As a Forest School Lead, you will work closely with resource base staff, the Trust’s Sustainability Lead and Inclusion Team, as well as the whole school community to support the delivery of an ambitious and bespoke provision, which will successfully meet the needs of the pupils and enable them to achieve the best possible outcomes regardless of their circumstance or background.

Within the Trust you will have:

Opportunities to share ideas and improve both your own and the specialist base practice

Your professional ambitions actively encouraged and supported

Opportunities to work with colleagues across other schools within the Trust


The Trust will provide:

The opportunity to make a real difference to the lives of children, many of whom are disadvantaged

A supportive team

Quality resources and rich environments, to enable you to support the development of a personalised approach to Forest School provision


Excellent CPD to support you in your career development

The Role

We are seeking to appoint an outstanding SEND Forest School Lead to work full time across schools within drb Ignite MAT, supporting the pupils of the newly opening Communication and Interaction Specialist Bases. This is an exciting opportunity to shape and deliver a high-quality outdoor learning offer for pupils with special educational needs and disabilities, with a particular focus on children with complex communication and interaction needs, including autism spectrum condition (ASC).

The successful candidate will lead inclusive, therapeutic, and engaging Forest School provision primarily for the pupils within the Specialist Bases, that supports pupils’ communication, emotional regulation, sensory needs, confidence, independence and social development. They will collaborate closely with school leaders, SENDCos, teachers, support staff and families to ensure that outdoor learning contributes meaningfully to pupils’ individual outcomes and wider inclusion.

  • This role aligns strongly with drb Ignite Trust’s vision that all pupils achieve the highest standard of educational outcomes regardless of circumstance or background.
  • The post holder will embody the Trust’s values through optimism and high expectations, trust and integrity, valuing every contribution, noticing acts of kindness and celebrating success.
  • You will be committed to inclusive practice and to ensuring that pupils with the most complex needs are enabled to thrive through carefully planned, relationship-based and evidence-informed provision.
  • You will align your practice with drb Ignite Trust’s sustainability objectives and climate action plan.

Please contact our Sustainability Manager Steven Owens, for any clarifications of the job role via sowens@drbignitemat.org

We look forward to hearing from you.

For further information about the role please see the attached job description and person specification.

Closing date: 9am Monday 7th December 2026

Interviews: Monday 14th December 2026

Please note that CVs are not accepted.

Please note: In line with Safer Recruitment Practice, a minimum of two references will be sought for shortlisted candidates prior to interview. One reference must be the candidate’s current/most recent employer. The Trust is absolutely committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and adults through its safer recruitment processes. The Trust expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. An enhanced DBS check will be required for this post.

We encourage all applicants to review our Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy, which outlines our commitment to the safety and wellbeing of students.

As part of our due diligence an online search will be carried out for all shortlisted candidates.

Rehabilitation of Offenders

This post is exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 and the amendments to the Exceptions Order 1975, 2013 and 2020. Which means that when applying for certain jobs and activities certain spent convictions and cautions are ‘protected’, so they do not need to be disclosed to employers, and if they are disclosed, employers cannot take them into account.

Further information about filtering offences can be found in the DBS filtering guide.

This post is covered by Part 7 of the Immigration Act (2016).

You can work from home or one of our Central Europe offices (Bratislava, Brno, Prague) on a full-time basis. The base salary range for this position is 1 520 000 - 1 900 000 CZK. The pay range actually offered will take into account a variety of potential factors considered in compensation, including but not limited to skills, qualifications, geographic location, accomplishments, experience, credentials, internal equity and business needs, and may vary from the range listed above. Are you ready to grow with us?

 What tech stack do we have for you?

• Kubernetes (GKE), Terraform, GitLab

• Google Cloud, including a wide range of managed products such as Cloud SQL, BigQuery, Bigtable, Dataflow, and Pub/Sub

• Self-hosted stack: MongoDB, Kafka, Elasticsearch, Etcd, Victoria Metrics, InfluxDB, Sentry

• Python, Golang

 Minimum requirements:

 At least 5 years of production experience with:

• Kubernetes - we are looking for an engineer who not only deploys applications to a cluster, but also understands what is happening behind the scenes and can operate 24x7 production

• GCP (preferred)/AWS/Azure - our solution is built on top of the GCP platform. Candidate should be comfortable working with public cloud, understand the risks and benefits associated with running applications in the public cloud, be familiar with infrastructure as a code principle, and have the ability to make design choices between using cloud-managed solutions versus self-hosted alternatives

• Python/Go - you should be able to read and understand code with confidence, and to review and evaluate AI-generated Python code for correctness, security, and fit. Hands-on coding skills matter less than before, but you should still be able to develop custom tooling when needed, with or without AI assistance

 If you don’t meet these requirements, don’t worry; take a look at the Senior DevOps position - Czechia: https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/bloomreach/jobs/8329244 , Slovakia: https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/bloomreach/jobs/8329243

 How to know if you are a good fit:

 The qualifications outlined below serve as a guide to determine if your skills and experience align with the requirements of this position:

• Design and Specification : You turn loosely defined problems into designs and specifications that others can execute. You write design proposals, weigh trade-offs between managed and self-hosted solutions, and review the designs of others.

• Cross-team Leadership : You have led projects spanning multiple teams, from scoping and planning through delivery, coordinating engineers who do not report to you.

• Independent Delivery : You take a specified maintenance or project task and drive it to completion on your own. AI assistants are a given part of your toolkit, but you always understand and can explain how and why every change was made.

• AI as a Tool, Not a Replacement : You use AI assistants to work faster, not to hand your work over. You understand what the AI produced, question and verify it, and steer it toward the outcome you want rather than accepting whatever it gives you. You stay in control and remain accountable for everything you ship.

• Continuous Learning : You have a keen interest in Kubernetes and related technologies, as demonstrated by your active engagement in reading and staying up to date on them.

• Conference Participation : You have participated in DevOps-related conferences, showcasing your commitment to continuous learning and networking in the field.

• Configuration Proficiency : You have hands-on experience configuring pod/container security context, network policies, roles and role bindings, pod affinity, host path, pod disruption budgets, priority classes, node taints, to name a few.

• Resource Optimization : You have analyzed resource usage of applications hosted on a cluster and implemented or suggested changes to resource requests/limits, Horizontal Pod Autoscalers (HPAs), or Vertical Pod Autoscalers (VPAs).

• Cluster Management : You have a deep understanding of the clusters you manage, including the types of machines used in node pools, the reasons for their selection, which cluster features are enabled or disabled, the cluster version, and the node autoscaling configuration. You have successfully upgraded the Kubernetes cluster versions without interrupting live applications hosted on the cluster.

• Terraform Proficiency : You have written a Terraform module with multiple interconnected resources.

• Monitoring and Alerting : You have experience setting up monitoring systems and configuring alerts. On-duty experience is preferred, along with experience with Grafana and Prometheus.

• DevOps and CI/CD Experience : You have experience with DevOps, Orchestration/Configuration Management, and Continuous Integration technologies, including Terraform, GitLab, Ansible, and Docker.

• Team Onboarding and Training : You have experience with onboarding and training new team members, demonstrating your leadership skills and commitment to team growth.

 About your team:

 The Infrastructure team operates and maintains Bloomreach Engagement core infrastructure built on Google Cloud with security, high availability, costs, and scalability in mind. Our vision is to identify and implement opportunities to achieve a robust, reliable, and efficient infrastructure and development platform. We strongly support DevOps culture: each team is responsible for releasing, operating, and monitoring their own applications.

 The role of the Infrastructure Team is to provide a strong foundation upon which all teams can build, for example, manage big infrastructure components like Kubernetes, databases, and cloud components in Google Cloud. An important role of the team is also to provide support to developers, review design proposals, validate the performance and availability of applications, and sometimes even develop new core application components such as logging or authorization.

 Tasks and responsibilities:

 In the position of Staff DevOps Engineer, you’d be expected to work with other Engineering teams to design sustainable infrastructure, microservice solutions, and an efficient and robust production environment. Additionally, you’ll be working on a variety of tasks and projects, including automating tools and infrastructure to reduce manual work, monitoring applications and participating in an on-call rotation as required.

 You’ll own the design and specification of infrastructure initiatives, break them down into tasks the team can execute, and lead projects that span multiple engineering teams. AI assistants are a given part of your toolkit, and you retain full understanding of, and responsibility for, what gets shipped.

 The ideal candidate will be passionate about learning new things, creative, willing to take the initiative, and able to think outside the box to solve problems strategically.

title: CLX Property Advocate, UK
description:
We're looking for a CLX Property Advocate to help our UK customers through some of the most stressful moments they'll face as policyholders. You'll join our Claims Experience team and own property claims from first report to resolution, keeping every interaction fast, fair, and caring. This role is remote, and you'll need to be online during UK working hours.

We believe three things matter for every role at Lemonade: drive to push through challenges, efficiency that keeps standards high while moving fast, and adaptability that lets you pivot with data and AI insights. These aren't buzzwords, they're how we actually work.

Our AI-first approach isn't just a tagline either. We're building the future of insurance with AI at the center, and we need people who are genuinely excited to learn and grow alongside these tools.

  • Own the complex and sensitive claims where judgment, empathy, and experience matter most.

  • Prioritize your daily caseload so no customer waits longer than they should.

  • Partner with fellow advocates to flag edge cases and shape how we handle them.

  • Spot patterns in recurring claim types and share them with the team to build smarter processes.

  • Keep our tone warm and human in every conversation, especially the hard ones.

What you'll need

  • Hands-on experience handling complex and large claims, preferably in property insurance

  • Working knowledge of UK consumer insurance rules, including the fair treatment of customers

  • Strong written and spoken English, with the ability to explain a complex claim simply

  • A customer-first mindset, plus the empathy and patience to stay steady when someone is stressed or frustrated

  • Comfort in a fast-paced environment where priorities shift, and real curiosity about how AI tools can sharpen your work

  • A CII qualification, complex building claims experience, or time at a digital-first insurer (a bonus, not a must)

  • Ability to work in a remote environment

title: Actuarial Associate, UK
description:
We’re looking for a technically savvy Actuarial Pricing Associate to join the UK team and support pricing adequacy, accuracy, and competitiveness of our European products. You will contribute your actuarial expertise as part of an interdisciplinary team that includes data scientists, insurance Product and Underwriting professionals. Working in collaboration, you’ll help develop and implement new pricing capabilities that blend actuarial approaches with predictive modeling, machine learning, and artificial intelligence.

In this role you’ll

  • Help shape our UK pricing strategy, balancing profitable growth, competitive prices and great customer outcomes.

  • Turn trading data into action, digging into conversion, retention, risk mix and profitability to spot opportunities and explain what’s changing.

  • Build a deep understanding of competitor pricing and our position on price comparison websites, using those insights to improve how we price.

  • Own pricing changes from idea to launch, testing their impact and tracking what happens once they’re live.

  • Partner with Data Science, Product and Underwriting to bring together predictive models, customer behaviour and commercial insight.

  • Bring your UK insurance expertise to our global team, sharing knowledge and challenging assumptions to help us make better decisions.

  • Help build a faster, smarter pricing engine through automation, experimentation and thoughtful use of AI.

  • Further your actuarial education through industry research and stay on top of changing regulatory requirements

What you’ll need

  • 3–5 years of UK personal lines pricing experience, including hands-on commercial or street pricing.

  • A strong understanding of how the UK insurance market works, with practical experience of price comparison websites, competitor pricing and customer behaviour.

  • A track record of turning analysis into pricing changes that deliver measurable results.

  • Strong SQL and Python or R skills, with confidence exploring data independently and checking that your conclusions hold up.

  • Commercial judgement and curiosity: you ask good questions, challenge assumptions and connect the numbers to what’s happening in the market.

  • Clear communication skills and enthusiasm for sharing your UK market knowledge with colleagues across the business.

  • Working knowledge of UK pricing/insurance regulations

  • Enthusiasm for learning and working with AI, and exploring how it can improve the way we price and work.

  • UK home pricing experience is a strong plus, as are actuarial qualifications and experience with demand modelling or optimisation.

  • Ability to work from our London office.

  • Commitment in obtaining FIA (Fellow of the Institute of Actuaries) or FFA (Fellow of the Faculty of Actuaries)

  • Master’s degree in mathematics / econometrics / actuarial science / related field preferred

title: VP, Sales EMEA
description:
StackAdapt is the leading technology company that empowers marketers to reach, engage, and convert audiences with precision. With 465 billion automated optimizations per second, the AI-powered StackAdapt Marketing Platform seamlessly connects brand and performance marketing to drive measurable results across the entire customer journey. The most forward-thinking marketers choose StackAdapt to orchestrate high-impact campaigns across programmatic advertising and marketing channels.

We are seeking an experienced Vice President, Sales – EMEA to lead StackAdapt's sales organization across the UK, Spain, Germany, France and the UAE. This leader will own the regional sales strategy and lead a geographically dispersed team of sales leaders and Sales Managers, with London as the hub and team members in each of our continental European and Middle Eastern markets.

This role is responsible for driving revenue growth across independent agencies and brands. In the UK, that means owning new and existing brands and independent agencies. In Spain, Germany, France and the UAE, it means building and scaling markets where teams sell across segments, inclusive of holding companies. The ideal candidate brings deep DSP and programmatic advertising experience, strong relationships across the EMEA advertising ecosystem, and a proven track record of leading high-performing sales organizations across multiple markets.

This leader will partner closely with UK Enterprise Sales leadership, Client Services, Agency Development, Marketing, Product, Solutions, Inventory Partnerships, Sales Enablement, Data & Analytics, and Revenue Operations to strengthen StackAdapt's market position and accelerate growth across EMEA.

StackAdapt is a remote-first company; however, our sales teams operate regionally. For this role, we are prioritising candidates located in the UK or EU, ideally in commutable distance to our London hub.

What You'll Be Doing:

EMEA Sales Strategy & Growth

  • Own and execute the sales strategy for the UK, Spain, Germany, France and the UAE, with accountability for regional revenue growth, new customer acquisition, and expansion within existing accounts.
  • Develop differentiated strategies, organizational structure, and hiring needs for independent agencies, holding companies, and direct brands, reflecting how each buys and how buying behavior varies across markets.
  • Build market-by-market playbooks. Germany, France, UAE, and Spain each have distinct agency landscapes, buying cycles and privacy expectations.
  • Establish a consistent regional operating rhythm for targets, pipeline health, forecasting, territory strategy and overall sales performance.
  • Partner with Finance, Legal and Deal Desk to maintain deal quality and sustainable commercial terms.

Leadership & Team Development

  • Lead and develop a geographically dispersed organization of sales leaders and Account Executives across the UK, continental Europe and the UAE, selling across independent agencies and direct brands.
  • Build leadership depth in each market and set clear expectations, operating rhythms and accountability across time zones and cultures.
  • Recruit, coach and develop high-performing sales talent, including the first local leaders in expansion markets, while fostering a connected regional culture.
  • Support the team on strategic opportunities, complex negotiations and executive customer relationships.

Customer & Market Leadership

  • Build executive-level relationships across independent agencies, holding companies, and brands in each market.
  • Partner with UK Enterprise Sales leadership on multi-market and Holding Company accounts, with a clear operating model to ensure a consistent StackAdapt service motion. Serve as a senior DSP and programmatic leader in strategic pitches, platform evaluations and competitive conversations.
  • Represent StackAdapt with senior customers, partners and industry stakeholders across EMEA.

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Partner across UK Enterprise Sales, Client Services, Agency Development, Product, Solutions, Marketing, Inventory Partnerships, Sales Enablement, Data & Analytics and Revenue Operations to execute an integrated EMEA go-to-market strategy.
  • Bring EMEA voice of customer and market insights into company strategy, product development and investment decisions, including regional privacy and data requirements.
  • Use data and market intelligence to identify growth opportunities, improve sales performance and prioritize resources across markets.

What You'll Bring to the Table

  • Experience balancing an established core business with building newer markets, and knowing when an account warrants an enterprise approach.
  • Significant sales leadership experience within a demand-side platform (DSP) or directly comparable programmatic advertising business.
  • Deep knowledge of the European and Middle Eastern programmatic advertising ecosystem and how agencies and brands evaluate and adopt DSPs.
  • Proven track record of owning and exceeding regional revenue targets across multiple EMEA markets.
  • Demonstrated success selling to independent agencies and direct brands, with exposure to Holding Company structures and agency trading relationships.
  • Experience leading geographically dispersed, multi-country sales teams and sales leaders, including hiring first local leaders in new markets.
  • Understanding of privacy-first selling, including GDPR and consent requirements that shape how brands and agencies buy.
  • Strong operational discipline across forecasting, pipeline management, territory planning and performance management.
  • Comfort working across time zones with North American leadership and regional teams.
  • Executive presence and the ability to influence customers, cross-functional partners and senior leadership.

The compensation range listed for this role reflects the expected base salary for candidates located in the posting country based on a global rate. It is informed by market data and the approved budget for this position. StackAdapt maintains different compensation ranges for roles across other countries and regions, and final offers will be aligned to the candidate’s current location. We do not ask candidates about current or prior salary history, and we will not use such information, if volunteered, in setting an offer.

This range represents base salary only. Depending on the role, candidates may also be eligible for additional compensation such as annual bonuses, commissions, equity awards, and a comprehensive benefits package.

£1—£1 GBP

title: Enterprise Account Executive - Public Sector
description:
SLSQ127R39

Location: Northern Ireland or Scotland, with regular UK&I team collaboration
Reports to: Head of Public Sector Enterprise, UK&I

Do you want to help solve the public sector’s toughest challenges with Data and AI? That is what we do every day at Databricks.

Databricks is looking for a senior-level Enterprise Account Executive to own and grow our Public Sector business across the Republic of Ireland and Scotland. You will inherit an established book of strategic government accounts, with a clear mandate to protect and expand that base while building new relationships and opening net-new opportunities across departments and agencies we do not yet serve in partnership with our growth team.

This is a succession role: you will step into relationships and momentum that already exist, building trust quickly with current stakeholders while creating a strategic go-to-market plan for the wider Irish public sector. You will develop a deep understanding of national and departmental government priorities, identify where Data and AI can help solve the country’s most important challenges, and translate those opportunities into measurable customer outcomes and sustainable growth.

Working closely with government stakeholders, internal teams, cloud providers, and strategic partners, you will deepen consumption in existing accounts and extend Databricks’ footprint across the Republic of Ireland.

The impact you will have

  • Build and execute a strategic, Ireland-wide go-to-market plan that prioritises government agendas, departments, agencies, use cases, partners, and routes to market that can create sustainable growth.
  • Take ownership of an existing portfolio of Irish Government strategic accounts, maintaining continuity with current stakeholders and expanding usage of the Databricks Intelligence Platform.
  • Identify and pursue net-new opportunities across departments and agencies that are not yet engaged with Databricks, building a healthy pipeline alongside your existing account portfolio in partnership with our growth team.
  • Develop a clear view of national and departmental priorities and translate them into compelling Data and AI value propositions, executive conversations, business cases, and qualified opportunities.
  • Map and engage the full range of buying centres within each account, building champions, guiding opportunities forward, and compressing decision cycles.
  • Run a consumption-led sales motion, using demand plans to prioritise the highest-value use cases in each account and grow usage over time rather than closing one-off deals.
  • Manage a portfolio that spans quick wins and longer, complex public-sector sales cycles simultaneously.
  • Build and defend a strong renewal and expansion motion within existing accounts as a foundation for new growth.
  • Orchestrate cross-functional and partner resources; including professional services, training, systems integrators, and hyperscaler co-sell teams to maximise account impact.
  • Represent Databricks credibly with senior government stakeholders, acting as a trusted advisor.
  • Maintain a relentless customer focus by delivering technical and business outcomes through the Databricks Intelligence Platform.

What we look for

  • A strong track record of quota attainment or over-achievement selling into public-sector accounts, ideally in Ireland or a comparable market.
  • Demonstrated ability to build a territory or market-level go-to-market strategy from the ground up, create new demand, and drive growth beyond an existing account base.
  • Experience managing an existing strategic account portfolio through a transition, building trust quickly with inherited relationships while also prospecting for new ones.
  • Working knowledge of Irish Government structures, national and departmental priorities, procurement frameworks, and how public-sector technology decisions are funded, approved, and implemented.
  • Sales experience in cloud software, data platforms, open-source technology, Data and AI, or a related enterprise technology market.
  • Experience selling usage-based or consumption-based models and co-selling with AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud.
  • Comfort running both land-and-expand motions in existing accounts and greenfield business development across new departments and agencies.
  • The ability to identify relevant use cases and buying centres within an opportunity, increasing Databricks’ impact and business value across an organisation.
  • Experience co-developing business cases and building relationships with C-level executives and senior civil-service stakeholders.
  • A demonstrated ability to build effective champions, collaborative account teams, and strategic partnerships that support execution of a territory plan.
  • Experience using structured sales methodologies, such as MEDDPICC, Value Selling, or similar, with disciplined and accurate forecasting.
  • A consistent track record of delivering results and making meaningful contributions to customers, teams, and the wider business.
  • Eligibility for security clearance; existing clearance is an advantage.

About Databricks

Databricks is the Data and AI company. More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever, and 70% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data + AI Platform to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics and agents. Headquartered in San Francisco with 30+ offices around the globe, Databricks offers a unified platform that includes Genie, Lakebase, Agent Bricks, Lakeflow, Lakehouse, and Unity Catalog. To learn more, follow Databricks on LinkedIn, X, YouTube, and Instagram.

title: Commercial Legal Counsel (Contractor)
description:
Liftoff is a leading AI-powered performance marketing platform for the mobile app economy. Our end-to-end technology stack helps app marketers acquire and retain high-value users, while enabling publishers to maximize revenue across programmatic and direct demand.

Liftoff’s solutions, including Accelerate, Direct, Monetize, Intelligence, and Vungle Exchange, support over 6,600 mobile businesses across 74 countries in sectors such as gaming, social, finance, ecommerce, and entertainment. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in Redwood City, CA, Liftoff has a diverse, global presence.

Liftoff is looking for a Commercial Legal Counsel that will assist the in-house legal department with Insertion Orders (Agreements), third party contracts and other legal needs. This position will support the Commercial, Finance and Accounting teams, located around the world.

As a Commercial Legal Counsel at Liftoff, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring the seamless execution of contracts that drive our business forward. You will be at the intersection of legal expertise, meticulous organization, and collaborative teamwork. Your responsibilities will encompass contract drafting, negotiation, process improvement and training. As an essential part of our team, you'll contribute to the foundation of our business relationships and help us navigate the complex world of contracts with precision and efficiency. If you're passionate about detail-oriented work, contract law, and making a meaningful impact, this role is your opportunity to shine. Join us in shaping the way we manage contracts and elevate our commitment to excellence.

Responsibilities:

  • Draft, review, and negotiate a wide range of contracts, including vendor agreements, customer contracts, and licensing agreements, to ensure compliance with company policies and legal requirements.
  • Collaborate with internal teams, including legal, sales/commercial, product, engineering, finance and accounting to understand contract terms, resolve issues, and provide guidance on contractual matters.
  • Maintain an organized and up-to-date contract ticketing system, respond to each contract ticket in a timely manner and track contract milestones and deadlines.
  • Assist in contract compliance, addressing any deviations or breaches.
  • Assist in the development and improvement of contract templates and standard clauses.
  • Support the contract approval process, ensuring proper authorization and documentation.
  • Provide guidance and training to employees on contract-related matters and best practices.
  • Stay updated on relevant laws and regulations impacting contract management.

Requirements:

  • 5-10 Years of experience
  • Bachelor's degree in Law, or a related field.
  • Proven experience as a Contracts Counsel/Legal Counsel or in a similar role.
  • Strong understanding of contract law and legal terminology.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Detail-oriented with exceptional organizational and time management abilities.
  • Proficiency in contract management software or tools.
  • Ability to work collaboratively in a cross-functional team environment globally.
  • Prior experience in ad-tech is a plus.

Location:

This position is based in London or remotely within the United Kingdom, occasionally going into the office.

This position is a contract position with the potential to become a full-time employee. The expected hours of work required for this position are 35 to 40 hours per week, with occasional early evening hours for team meetings, as the manager is located in our Redwood City office in California.

description:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

We are seeking a highly motivated and analytical individual to join our Growth Analytics International team. This team plays a crucial role in conducting research, monitoring performance, and running experiments to develop exceptional products for both consumers and merchants while driving long-term growth for the business. As Affirm continues expanding into new international markets, this role will be instrumental in establishing the operational analytics framework for new launches, beginning with Australia and expanding into future international markets. The ideal candidate will possess strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, a collaborative mindset, an eagerness to learn, and the patience to tackle complex challenges.

Our team takes an end-to-end business analytics perspective, partnering across the organization to develop recommendations and solutions that enable the business to successfully execute its growth and profitability strategies. This role requires someone who can combine analytical rigor with business acumen to influence decisions and drive measurable outcomes.

What you’ll do

  • Establish and evolve the operational analytics framework for new international markets, ensuring scalable measurement, reporting, and decision-making capabilities as we expand globally.
  • Operate with a business owner mindset by proactively identifying opportunities through analysis and product sense to enhance user experience, growth, and profitability.
  • Own business problems from end to end by translating analytical insights into recommendations and optimization strategies that support business growth, profitability, and operational excellence.
  • Take ownership of the end-to-end analytics process: define success metrics, generate insights and hypotheses, track performance, and create intuitive dashboards and reports that can be easily shared across the organization. Develop scalable analytics solutions and data models.
  • Tackle ambiguous problems by identifying the core hypotheses and designing actionable experiments to validate product-market fit and economic viability.
  • Translate analytical findings into clear and compelling narratives and business cases for leadership to inform decision-making.
  • Spearhead weekly cross-functional metric reviews, collaborating with partners to conduct deep dives into significant metric shifts and suggest actionable steps.
  • Partner effectively across Product, Risk, Finance, Commercial, and Operations to align strategies and execute against business objectives.
  • Foster strong cross-functional relationships and establish yourself as a trusted advisor to team members.
  • Mentor and guide junior analysts to deliver high-impact work that drives business results.

What we look for:

  • Passion to redefine the lending and financial industry for the better.
  • Strong understanding of the consumer lending and credit industry, including lending economics, portfolio performance, and credit metrics. Experience supporting international lending markets, particularly Europe and/or APAC, is highly desirable.
  • Demonstrated ability to balance growth objectives with profitability and develop data-driven growth strategies.
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in a quantitatively rigorous subject area such as statistics, mathematics, finance, or economics.
  • 5+ years of proven success in a cross-functional analytical role.
  • Practical and theoretical knowledge of A/B testing.
  • Experience with SQL and performing statistical analysis using Python.
  • Experience simultaneously balancing multiple workstreams and prioritizing an analytics roadmap.
  • Demonstrated curiosity and a growth mindset, with hands-on experience using AI-powered tools such as Cursor, Claude, or similar assistants to accelerate analysis, automate workflows, enhance problem-solving, and advocate for AI adoption across analytical workflows.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to influence both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Comfortable partnering across multiple cross-functional teams, particularly Product, Risk, Commercial, Finance, and Operations.
  • Ability to think creatively and critically while thriving in a fast-paced, dynamic, and often ambiguous work environment.
  • Willingness to go out of your way to help teammates, with humility and a team-first mindset.
  • Previous experience mentoring and guiding junior analysts.

Compensation & Benefits

Pay Grade - M
Equity Grade - 5

Employees new to Affirm typically come in at the start of the pay range. Affirm focuses on providing a simple and transparent pay structure which is based on a variety of factors, including location, experience and job-related skills.

Base pay is part of a total compensation package that may include monthly stipends for health, wellness and tech spending, and benefits (including 100% subsidized medical coverage, dental and vision for you and your dependents). In addition, the employees may be eligible for equity rewards offered by Affirm Holdings, Inc. (parent company).

GBR base pay range per year: £113,000 - £161,000

Location - Remote UK

#LI-Remote

Remote-first with flexibility built in
Affirm is proud to be a remote-first company. Most roles can be done from almost anywhere within the country of employment. Some positions may occasionally require in-person work at an Affirm office, and a few are office-based due to the nature of the work. All new hires will be invited to attend an in-person onboarding experience.

Benefits designed for you
Our benefits reflect our commitment to care, transparency, and flexibility. Here are a few highlights:

  • Health coverage at no cost: We cover 100% of premiums for employees and their dependents.
  • Spending stipends: Monthly stipends support your tech setup, and the ability to choose health and wellness options that are right for you.
  • Time off to recharge: Flexible time off and generous holiday calendars help you rest when you need to.
  • Own a piece of what you build: Our employee stock purchase plan (ESPP) lets you buy Affirm stock at a discount.

We’re committed to providing an inclusive interview process, including accommodations for candidates with disabilities. If you need support, we’re happy to help.

For positions based in San Francisco or Los Angeles: Affirm considers qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, as required by law.

By clicking "Submit Application," you acknowledge that you have read Affirm's Global Candidate Privacy Notice and consent to the use of your personal information as described.

title: Principal ML Platform Engineer
description:
Synthesia is the world’s leading AI video platform for business, used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. Founded in 2017, the company is headquartered in London, with offices and teams across Europe and the US.

As AI continues to shape the way we live and work, Synthesia develops products to enhance visual communication and enterprise skill development, helping people work better and stay at the center of successful organizations.

Following our recent Series E funding round, where we raised $200 million, our valuation stands at $4 billion. Our total funding exceeds $530 million from premier investors including Accel, NVentures (Nvidia's VC arm), Kleiner Perkins, GV, and Evantic Capital, alongside the founders and operators of Stripe, Datadog, Miro, and Webflow.

We’re looking for a Principal Engineer to join the ML Platform team at Synthesia.

Our team builds and operates the systems that allow researchers and product teams to train, serve, and deploy generative models reliably and efficiently. This includes research infrastructure, production serving systems, internal tooling, and the platform interfaces that connect them. A growing part of our mission is making these systems more automation-friendly and agent-oriented, so that workflows can increasingly be operated through reliable tooling rather than manual effort.

We’re looking for a strong generalist with a systems mindset:

  • someone who is comfortable working across infrastructure, backend systems, and tooling, and who has seen ML systems in practice.

  • this is not a pure ML Engineer role. We’re especially interested in people who think deeply about reliability, scalability, performance, and resource efficiency in complex production environments.

This is a hands-on IC role with significant ownership. You’ll help shape how our ML platform evolves as we scale the number of models, workloads, tools and teams relying on it.

What you’ll do

  • Design and improve the platform systems that support model training, evaluation, and production serving.

  • Build infrastructure and tooling that make ML workloads more reliable, scalable, and cost-efficient.

  • Develop internal tools and workflows that are easy to operate both by humans and by agents.

  • Work on the architecture behind how models are deployed, served, and operated across research and product environments.

  • Improve how we schedule, monitor, and debug workloads running on GPUs and cloud infrastructure.

  • Develop internal tools and abstractions and agentic systems that reduce operational overhead for researchers and engineers.

  • Drive improvements across observability, automation, reliability, and developer experience.

  • Collaborate closely with researchers and product engineers to understand pain points and turn them into robust platform capabilities.

  • Contribute to technical direction and make pragmatic architectural tradeoffs as the platform grows.

You’ll thrive in this role if you have

  • Strong experience building or operating production systems with a focus on reliability, scalability, and maintainability.

  • A systems mindset: you naturally think in terms of bottlenecks, failure modes, interfaces, resource usage, and long-term operability.

  • Solid hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure, Linux, and infrastructure automation.

  • Experience with Kubernetes and operating distributed workloads in production.

  • Strong coding skills, ideally in Python or similar languages used for backend systems and tooling.

  • Strong judgment around where automation adds leverage, and where human control and reliability matter most.

  • Experience building internal platforms, developer tooling, or infrastructure abstractions used by other engineers.

  • Comfort working in ambiguous environments and taking ownership of open-ended technical problems.

  • A pragmatic approach: you care about solving the right problem well, not over-engineering.

Particularly relevant experience

  • Operating ML infrastructure or model serving systems in production.

  • Supporting research or data-intensive workloads.

  • Working with GPU-based systems or other performance-sensitive infrastructure.

  • Experience with observability and debugging in distributed systems.

  • Familiarity with Terraform, Datadog, GitHub Actions, or similar tools.

Bonus points for

  • Experience building agentic or LLM-powered internal tools.

  • Experience with workflow orchestration systems such as Temporal.

  • Experience working at the boundary between research and production engineering.

  • Familiarity with performance optimization, scheduling, or resource allocation problems.

  • Experience building lightweight product or developer-facing tools.

title: Group Financial Controller
description:
Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.

The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing.

We are hiring a Group Financial Controller.

The ideal candidate has a deep passion for systems accounting, a track record of preparing finance functions for public markets and an innovative mindset that leverages technology and AI to build efficient and robust accounting workflows.
The Accounting team ensures the integrity of our financial information and serves as the primary stewards of the business’ financial health. They design and operate a governance framework underpinned by robust policies, controls and systems to provide oversight and challenge to the business. The team is responsible for timely and accurate reporting and exercises judgment when necessary based on a commitment to conservative and accurate reporting, a deep understanding of accounting principles and insights into our business.

We are looking for a professionally qualified accounting leader who has a deep sense of right and wrong, high integrity, and a strong sense of responsibility, understanding that the accuracy of their work is critical to the entire Company. 

You are a methodical, detail-oriented, and process-driven problem-solver who enjoys investigating discrepancies to find their root cause. You are resilient under pressure, particularly during month-end and year-end closes, and motivated by the goal of achieving a perfect, timely, and reliable result.

Perhaps unusually we prefer a leader with deep personal interest in the software and technology industry, and some data analytics, AI and ideally software engineering experience.

Location: This role is home-based in EMEA time zones, with the option to be based in our London office. It will report to our Chief Financial Officer.

The role entails

  • Ensuring strong understanding of the risks associated with our processes and systems and leading the development and implementation of controls to mitigate those risks
  • Leading the development and identification of areas of improvement of Canonical’s policies and procedures that will enable the business to scale efficiently
  • Driving the implementation of the Canonical’s policies and procedures and the monitoring of compliance 
  • Supporting multi-functional change projects designed to enhance systems, processes, and data accuracy
  • Managing reviews of weekly, month-end, year-end processes from balance sheet reconciliations to management accounts and statutory accounts preparation to ensure timely and accurate reporting of financial information
  • Ensuring accuracy and completeness of the recording and reporting of financial data and transactions to ensure that the Company maintains robust accounting records
  • Upholding the Company’s accounting and approval processes and controls across the organization
  • Managing external audits 
  • Developing a strong understanding of the evolving regulatory frameworks and jurisdictions in which Canonical operates and lead the assurance of Canonical’s compliance with such regulatory requirements
  • Driving projects associated with upgrading or implementing new finance systems and sensible AI adoption in the team
  • Developing professional relationships and manage communications with both internal and external stakeholders - customers, vendors, tax authorities and external advisers - including resolving questions and issues confidentially and in a timely manner
  • Managing or mentoring junior accounting staff, sharing knowledge and promoting best practices

What we are looking for in you

  • Exceptional academic track record from both high school and university
  • A strong academic background and professional qualification in Accounting or Finance (e.g. ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CPA, or equivalent)
  • Extensive practical IFRS knowledge and experience
  • Advanced Excel skills and strong data analysis capabilities
  • Excellent attention to detail and organizational skills, with the ability to prioritize and meet tight deadlines in a fast-paced setting
  • Confident communication and interpersonal skills, with the confidence to engage effectively with colleagues, management, customers, and external stakeholders
  • A proactive, analytical mindset with a genuine passion for finance and a drive for continuous improvement, process efficiency and professional development
  • Proven experience using enterprise-level accounting or ERP systems
  • Result-oriented, with a personal drive to meet and exceed commitments
  • Ability to travel internationally twice a year for company events up to two weeks long

Nice-to-have skills

  • Experience with NetSuite
  • Experience with Salesforce
  • Experience with a Big 4 Accounting Firm, or a Public company

What we offer colleagues

We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

  • Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person
  • Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year
  • Annual compensation review
  • Recognition rewards
  • Annual holiday leave
  • Maternity and paternity leave
  • Team Member Assistance Program & Wellness Platform
  • Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues
  • Priority Pass and travel upgrades for long-haul company events

About Canonical

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open-source projects and the platform for AI, IoT, and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence; in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since our inception in 2004.​ Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer

We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.

title: Member of Technical Staff (Robotics)
description:
We are an AI research lab building foundational intelligence for the physical world.

Our models are designed to solve complex real-world challenges, powering everything from intelligent robots to next-generation wearables and media.

We work at the intersection of world models, video generation, and robotics, building systems that represent complex environments, reason about objects and dynamics, and translate high-level AI intentions into smooth, efficient, safe, and responsive actions across a variety of robotic embodiments.

You will collaborate closely with ML researchers developing multimodal world models and generative systems, and with hardware teams and partners to ensure robotic platforms, sensing, and system dynamics behave optimally in real-world operation.

What You’ll Do

  • Build the Foundation: Collaborate with our world model team to build state-of-the-art training and simulation platform for robotics.

  • Build the "World": Develop persistent 3D/4D scene representations that maintain temporal consistency.

  • Drive Intelligence: Unlock advanced robotics planning and decision making through our in-house, cutting-edge world models.

  • Sim2Real: Ensure sensing and system dynamics perform reliably in high-stakes, real-world operations, where models think, simulate, and act.

  • Push Boundaries: Partner with top ML researchers to innovate on generative models and physical AGI.

Areas of Interest

We are particularly excited about candidates working on topics such as:

  • World models for embodied systems

  • 3D / 4D generative models

  • Robotics manipulation

  • Embodied AI

  • Multimodal AI

What We’re Looking For

  • Background in robotics, or computer vision

  • Experience with 3D perception, scene representations, or world models

  • Experience working with robotic systems, simulation, or real-world platforms

  • Strong programming skills (Python, C++, or similar)

  • Located in London or willing to relocate to London, UK

Ability to work across machine learning, perception, and robotics

Reka's Mission

Reka's mission is to build useful multimodal artificial intelligence and use it to empower organisations and businesses. We are a globally distributed foundation model startup, headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area, California. Embracing a remote-first approach, our team brings together top talent from around the world. Our founding team, along with many of our team members, has contributed to many of the breakthroughs in AI over the past decade.


Why Reka?

  • An Elite Team: Collaborate with top-tier engineers, researchers, operators from renowned organizations like Google DeepMind and Facebook AI Research (FAIR) and successful startups, driving innovation in cutting-edge AI technology.

  • Massive Market Opportunity: Be part of a rapidly growing industry poised to transform multiple sectors globally, offering the chance to make a significant impact.

  • Mission-Driven Environment: Work alongside a collaborative, mission-focused team dedicated to advancing AI for meaningful applications.

  • Inclusive and Open Culture: Thrive in an open and inclusive work environment that values diverse perspectives and fosters creativity.

  • Generous Benefits: Enjoy 5 weeks of paid leave to recharge, comprehensive healthcare benefits including vision and dental, and additional perks that support your well-being.

  • Visa Support: We provide visa assistance for UK employees to ensure a smooth transition and support your career with us.

title: Lecturer- Inclusive Learning Performing Arts and Life Skills
description:
Join Hertford Regional College as a Lecturer in Inclusive Learning Performing Arts & Life Skills.

You will deliver high-quality, inclusive and aspirational teaching, learning and assessment across Performing Arts and Life Skills, supporting learners with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) within the Department of Inclusive Learning. The post holder will foster a safe, supportive and ambitious learning environment that places learners at the heart of everything, enabling them to develop the knowledge, skills, confidence and independence needed to thrive in adulthood. This will support learners to become active citizens, engage within their communities and progress towards further learning, supported employment or meaningful employment.

About HRC

HRC are a vibrant, dynamic further education college, recently graded a Good College by Ofsted, with students across two campuses, with ambitious growth and development targets.

HRC put people first – students, staff, the organisations that they partner with, and the local communities that they serve.

The HRC goal is to create a supportive environment for all staff in which they can develop their skills, progress their career and make a real difference in their local community. HRC ethos is evident in everything that they do and are always looking for new colleagues who share the HRC vision and values. As part of the HRC team, you will benefit from fantastic on-site facilities, exciting opportunities for career progression and relevant training opportunities to help you gain the additional skills that you need to reach your full potential.

About the Role

We are looking for an inspirational Lecturer with excellent organisational and programme management skills.

In this role, you will:

Our school values trustworthiness, helpfulness, inspiration, straightforwardness, and heart, and we're seeking a KS4 Lead for Science who embodies these principles. Manchester Communication Academy is deeply rooted in the community, committed to improving outcomes for all students.

The successful candidate will join a thriving Science department, where collaboration and innovation drive student success. With a focus on evidence-informed teaching practices, you'll have the opportunity to contribute to our ongoing improvement journey.

Our Trust:

Greater Manchester Academies Trust comprises Manchester Communication Academy, Manchester Communication Primary Academy, and Manchester Communication Research School. Our Trust is guided by five core values: trustworthiness, helpfulness, inspiration, straightforwardness, and heart.

Our primary aim is to mitigate the impact of disadvantage and ensure our students are equipped for successful and fulfilling adult lives.

MCA received Research School status in September 2019 and we are proud of the work that we conduct in partnership with the EEF and how this drives our teaching practice.

We seek individuals who resonate with our values and share our commitment to excellence. If you align with our ethos, we welcome your application.

The Science department at MCA has demonstrated consistent improvement year on year, achieving results significantly above the national average. Our curriculum is designed to challenge and engage students, fostering a lifelong passion for science while delivering commendable academic outcomes.

Collaborative planning ensures a balanced workload and promotes both teacher autonomy and consistency.

Our team comprises dedicated practitioners committed to ongoing professional development. You will join a department that embraces the latest pedagogical developments, supported by a structured CPD program led by our Teacher Educator, an EEF Research School Evidence Lead in Education.

We foster a supportive environment, emphasizing professional relationships and regular communication. Social events and celebrations further enrich our collaborative culture.

For further details about the role and our school, please refer to the attached Applicant Information Pack.

Application Deadline: 8am on 30th November 2026

Interested in Applying?

We view the application process as mutual; not only must you be the right fit for us, but the school must also be the right fit for you. If you're intrigued by this opportunity, feel free to reach out to discuss the role further.

Manchester Communication Academy is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. The successful candidate will be subject to an Enhanced Disclosure via the Disclosure and Barring Service

description:
We have an exciting opportunity for an experienced electrical installation professional to join our team at Stephenson College as a Lecturer in Electrical Installation.

This is an excellent opportunity for an industry professional who is passionate about developing others and wants to use their knowledge and experience to support the next generation of skilled electricians.

What we are looking for

  • We are seeking an enthusiastic and knowledgeable electrical installation professional who can combine strong technical expertise with a commitment to teaching, assessment and apprentice development.

You will ideally have:

  • Relevant industry experience in electrical installation, with a strong understanding of current installation practices, inspection and testing, and electrical safety.
  • The ability to explain technical concepts clearly and demonstrate practical skills to learners with different levels of knowledge and experience.
  • A strong commitment to health and safety and the promotion of safe working practices.
  • Good communication, organisational and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build positive relationships with apprentices, employers and colleagues.
  • An understanding of assessment, feedback and quality assurance within vocational education or apprenticeship delivery, or a willingness to develop these skills.
  • A commitment to supporting apprentices to achieve their full potential and progress into successful careers within the electrical installation industry.
  • Teaching and assessing qualifications, or a willingness to work towards the relevant qualifications, would be advantageous, subject to the requirements of the role.

This is an opportunity to make a real difference by helping develop the skilled electrical workforce needed by employers and the wider construction industry.
